summary.text: Jason Smith is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Missouri's 8th District and chairs the House Committee on Ways and Means.
A former attorney, real estate agent and small-business owner, he served in the Missouri House from 2005 to 2013 before winning a 2013 special election to Congress.
His congressional website describes him as a seventh-generation Missourian who is a fourth-generation owner of his family's farm.

paragraphs.text: Smith was born in St. Louis in 1980 and raised in Salem, Missouri, where he attended Salem High School and, according to his congressional website, was active in FFA.
He earned degrees in Agricultural Economics and Business Administration from the University of Missouri-Columbia, according to his website, and a J.D. from Oklahoma City University in 2004.
He worked as an attorney, real estate agent and small-business owner before holding public office.
Smith served in the Missouri House of Representatives (District 120) from 2005 to 2013, rising to Speaker Pro Tem according to his website.
The Missouri Republican Party chose him as its nominee in the 2013 special election to replace Jo Ann Emerson, and he won the June 4, 2013 general election with 67.1% of the vote.
In Congress, Smith sat on the Judiciary and Natural Resources committees in 2013-2014 and on Ways and Means from 2015.
According to his website, he was Conference Secretary of the House Republican leadership during President Trump's first term and became the top Republican on the House Budget Committee in 2021.
He became chairman of Ways and Means in January 2023, and his website says he was the youngest chair in modern times at age 42; in 2025-2026 he also chairs the Joint Committee on Taxation.
According to his website, he led the committee's work on the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, signed July 4, 2025.
Smith won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 86.0% of the vote over Gordon Heslop.
According to his congressional website, he attends Grace Community Church in Salem.
